description: Hello! My name is Om Joshi, and I have many interests, some of which is Astrophotography, flying RC planes, and rocketry. I'm open to anyone interested in joining, regardless of skill level, if you feel interested, please don't hesitate to reach out to me.
summary: Me and my team developed "Three Objects, Never Coming Home," a structured story-telling and informative slides, discussing the hardware dispersed along our solar system and beyond. This project reviews over 3 major instruments developed by NASA, the Apollo 15 moon rovers, NASA's Sojourner, and also NASA's famous Pioneer 10/11. Our project submission directly addresses NASA's storytelling challenge by contextualizing the pinnacle of Engineering and its trade-offs, including lunar module ascent weight limits, and lander batter exhaustion, that necessitated leaving these craft behind after fulfilling their requirements. This project is important as it explores abandoned hardware from regular "space debris," to genuine human achievement. It goes to show that each probe and instrument greatly contributed to humanity and proved interstellar escape capability.
details: "Three objects, never coming home," is a storytelling project for NASA to chronicle historic NASA objects spread across our solar system. This project goes over Pioneer 10/11; 2 deep space objects that will forever go into interstellar space, Sojourner, a mars rover that helped NASA for decades in aiding with information, then lastly, the Apollo 15 Lunar rovers, which helped astronauts traverse the moon with ease. By synthesizing complex/important historical missions to space, it highlights technological breakthroughs, like Autonomous vehicles, and deep space explorers millions of miles away. Built using AI tools and my teams joint effort, it frames these objects not as simple "space debris," but technological advancements and a permanent monument of NASA's/Humanities ingenuity and curiosity to understand what's beyond the Earth and beyond.
